panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Panel A displays a sagittal CT of the knee showing characteristic features of Sinding-Larsen-Johansson disease: an ossified fragment at the inferior pole of the patella and cortical irregularity, consistent with the case caption. B: Panel B displays a 3D CT reconstruction of the knee, providing anatomical context for the ossified fragment at the inferior pole of the patella, consistent with Sinding-Larsen-Johansson disease.

panels.figure_caption: CT of the knee demonstrating a chronic Sinding-Larsen–Johansson lesion. (A) Sagittal CT image showing an ossified fragment at the inferior pole of the patella with cortical irregularity and sclerosis. (B) Three-dimensional CT reconstruction illustrating the bony fragment in relation to the patella and tibial tuberosity. CT = computed tomography.
in_text_mentions: Computed tomography scan (2024): confirmed a well-defined osteochondrosis originating from the inferior pole of the patella, with minimal separation. No evidence of acute fracture or joint involvement was observed (Fig. 5).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Axial T2-weighted MRI image demonstrating key features of SLJS: focal bone marrow edema and cortical irregularity at the inferior pole of the patella, as specified in the caption. B: Sagittal T2-weighted MRI image demonstrating key features of SLJS: cortical irregularity and subchondral bone marrow edema at the patellar attachment, supporting the diagnosis.
panels.attribution_text: Alhamzah et al. Beyond conservative management: Surgical excision for symptomatic Sinding-Larsen-Johansson syndrome: A case report and literature review.. Medicine 2025. doi:10.1097/md.0000000000046792. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: Early MRI of the knee demonstrating a Sinding-Larsen–Johansson lesion at the inferior pole of the patella. (A) Axial T2-weighted image showing focal bone marrow edema and irregularity at the patellar attachment of the patellar tendon. (B) Sagittal T2-weighted image highlighting the cortical irregularity, subchondral edema, and associated soft tissue changes consistent with osteochondrosis. MRI = magnetic resonance imaging.
in_text_mentions: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) (January 2021): revealed mild thickening and signal alterations at the patellar tendon origin, with a small ossicle and subtle bone marrow edema, suggestive of early-stage SLJS (Fig. 3).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: MRI image (T2-weighted) of the knee showing progression of Sinding-Larsen-Johansson disease with cortical irregularity and fragmentation of the inferior patella pole. B: MRI image (T1-weighted) of the knee highlighting sclerosis and chronic bony remodeling at the patellar tendon insertion site, consistent with long-standing Sinding-Larsen-Johansson osteochondrosis.
panels.attribution_text: Alhamzah et al. Beyond conservative management: Surgical excision for symptomatic Sinding-Larsen-Johansson syndrome: A case report and literature review.. Medicine 2025. doi:10.1097/md.0000000000046792. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 4.
panels.figure_caption: Follow-up MRI of the knee performed 3 years after the initial study, demonstrating progression of the Sinding-Larsen–Johansson lesion at the inferior pole of the patella. (A) Sagittal T2-weighted image showing persistent cortical irregularity with increased fragmentation and surrounding marrow signal changes. (B) Sagittal T1-weighted image highlighting sclerosis and chronic bony remodeling at the patellar tendon insertion site, consistent with long-standing osteochondrosis. MRI = magnetic resonance imaging.
in_text_mentions: MRI (February 2024): showed interval progression, with increased tendon thickening, a larger ossified fragment, and more prominent infrapatellar fat pad edema (features indicative of chronic mechanical stress and impingement (Fig. 4)).
